CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
61-year-old male with history of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on January 22, 2013, who presents today for routine follow-up. Patient reports increased fatigue, which he attributes either to aging or end-of-day tiredness. Despite this, he remains quite active, cycling 20-30 miles on a road bike regularly, though he notes he previously could complete 40-mile rides. He experiences significant fatigue after long rides and must rest upon arriving home. He cycles with a friend, Tyler, who is older but now waits for him during rides, whereas previously the patient could keep pace or go faster.

Patient states he was informed that his aortic valve would last approximately 8 years. His last stress test was September 9, 2019. At now approximately 8 years post-surgery, he requested an echocardiogram to assess his valve function. He denies any significant changes since his last visit. He no longer follows up at Hopkins, receiving only intermittent local follow-up care.

Patient reports his wife and friends have noticed he purses his lips while breathing when walking. He is uncertain whether this is simply a habit or a concern of medical significance. Prior physicians have mentioned this finding. He denies associated wheezing.

Patient also discovered a small nodule on his right epididymis during self-examination. He states he is not particularly concerned but wanted medical evaluation.

Regarding mood and sleep, patient denies depression and describes himself as generally happy. He reports getting 6-7 hours of sleep nightly with variable schedule due to work and morning exercise routine. He has made reservations for twice-weekly 5:45 AM swimming sessions. Wife reports mild snoring but denies any episodes of apnea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for fatigue with physical exertion. Positive for pursed lip breathing without associated wheezing. Positive for mild snoring without reported apnea. Denies depression. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair (January 22, 2013)

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3: 50,000 units on Sundays; 2,000 units on other six days
Clindamycin prior to dental procedures

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is employed as a lecturer with work start time of 7:00 AM on teaching days. He maintains an active lifestyle with regular road biking of 20-30 miles and has made reservations for twice-weekly morning swimming sessions at 5:45 AM. He attempts to work out in the mornings. He is married. He denies depression and describes himself as overall a happy person.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing male, no acute distress
Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted with low exhalation phase, lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezing
Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3 mm palpable nodule on the epididymis, does not appear to be a varicocele; left testicle normal; no hernia
All other portions of physical examination normal

RESULTS
Labs from April 10, 2021:
Alkaline phosphatase: 156 (elevated)
Total cholesterol: 247 (elevated)
HDL: 66
LDL: 166 (elevated)
Triglycerides: 74
TSH: 2.68 (normal)
CBC: Unremarkable
Vitamin D: 94 (high end of normal)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Status post aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient doing well, asymptomatic, approximately 8 years post-surgery. Will order echocardiogram and stress test for further evaluation. Referral to cardiology with Dr. Vincent Sanchez recommended as primary cardiologist.

2. Elevated alkaline phosphatase: Most recent level 156. Likely related to bone health rather than hepatic disease. Labs to be obtained today including alkaline phosphatase and GGT. Results will be communicated via patient portal; patient will be called if results are significantly abnormal.

3. Pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase: Pulmonary function testing ordered for further evaluation.

4. Right testicular nodule (2-3 mm on epididymis): Referral to urology placed for evaluation including possible ultrasound.

5. Preventive health and immunizations: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended and will be scheduled for next month. COVID-19 vaccination completed (first dose January 15, 2021; second dose February 5, 2021).

6. Follow-up: Patient to return in one year for wellness visit. Earlier follow-up may be arranged after review of pending labs and studies. Patient to contact office with any questions or concerns.
